docs.title: One assignment, one current plan
docs.text:
AI Agents provides a shared operating model, reusable profiles and a local toolkit. People choose goals and accept consequential decisions. AI delivers bounded increments using the models, tools and permissions available in its host.

docs.title: Execution belongs to your host
docs.text:
Jörg selects relevant expertise. Delegation depends on host capabilities and permissions; the current session can otherwise use selected guidance directly. Inference may be local or remote according to your provider configuration.

The toolkit exports profiles and manages files. Its dashboard does not run models or synchronize project trackers or wikis. Recurring work needs an implemented runner and authorized host tools; the runner contract describes the requirements.

docs.title: Sources and published views
docs.text:
Edit canonical Markdown, then regenerate the index, relationships and website. This catalog site uses MkDocs. The Docusaurus guide applies to the customer's existing site. A root docs/ used for compiled Pages output stays generated.

The site renders profiles, the operating model and worked examples from canonical sources. The knowledge map uses explicit metadata and local links. Customer facts and private vault paths do not belong in this public toolkit.

docs.title: Work with AI as a teammate
docs.text:
Organize delivery around a clear outcome, an accountable owner and evidence. Give AI context and action scope for the assignment. Keep customer knowledge in customer-controlled systems so another person or agent can continue the work.

As implementation becomes faster with AI, goals, decision rights, feedback and shared knowledge need to remain explicit. This model makes those handoffs visible without asking people to maintain several copies of the same plan.

Use the workspace concept for the complete folder, YAML, decision, recovery and publication model. Optional local records now share workspace/ with project context; tracked delivery retains its existing issue or ticket.

docs.title: From business value to useful knowledge
docs.text:
Stage Human responsibility AI contribution Evidence Frame Choose outcome, scope and acceptance Inspect context and propose a bounded increment A Ready assignment Approve the plan when required Verify assumptions, comment and approve the current revision Revise the plan and preserve feedback A receipt in the existing planning home Deliver Resolve consequential questions Implement within scope and keep the plan accurate Focused code and relevant checks Review Review and decide acceptance Prepare a reviewable PR and explain remaining limits Required review and acceptance Learn and operate Choose follow-up work and assess impact Update affected knowledge and prepare iteration closeout Current knowledge, significant ADRs and observed results

These are activities, not mandatory separate agents, documents or meetings. Small changes take a direct path. Larger assignments need a visible plan and the people who can resolve consequential questions.

docs.title: Scale the process to uncertainty and consequence
docs.text:
Assignment Minimum useful flow Clear, reversible small change Inspect, implement, run relevant checks, report Uncertain feature or several affected boundaries Clarify the outcome, plan one complete slice, obtain required review, implement and verify Consequential migration or operational change Add the affected compatibility, rollout, recovery and observation checks; involve the accountable owner

Use product discovery when user value or the solution is uncertain. Compare the smallest software change with an existing capability or process improvement. State what would disprove the idea before investing in a larger implementation. A prototype, a passing build and a shipped feature each provide different evidence; none alone proves customer value.

docs.title: Let each project choose its tools
docs.text:
The project defines the system of record for each information type in a small workspace/workspace.yml, linked from AGENTS.md. Use an existing equivalent configuration when already present. The YAML owns the tooling map; the working agreement explains statuses, authority and process without duplicating locations.

Information Project specifies Accountable role Priority, iteration, status and assignment Tracker/board and project URL, e.g. Jira or GitHub Projects Product owner Live plan, acceptance and questions Work-item URL and the permitted section/field Work-item owner Implementation and verification Repository and PR/MR review location Author and reviewers Significant decisions and rationale ADR directory or designated decision space Decision maker Current domain, architecture and operational knowledge Repository, wiki or other customer-owned knowledge space Domain/technical owner Iteration outcomes Existing project update or report location Product owner Questions and approval Authorized channel, reviewer and scope of approval Relevant stakeholder

Name one authoritative location for each purpose and link related objects. Specify which statuses mean ready, reviewable and done, who may update which fields, and which access tools are available. A Jira ticket can own the entire live plan while GitHub hosts only the code and PR. There is no requirement to create a matching GitHub issue. Different ownership across tools is valid; two independently edited live plans are not.

Customer knowledge stays in customer-controlled systems. General expertise stays in AI Agents, and personal Second Brain notes stay in the private PARA vault. workspace/ can contain the knowledge itself or a compact index of its authoritative external homes. Docusaurus and the knowledge graph are optional views of the selected sources; external wiki synchronization is not implemented by this toolkit.

docs.title: Choose the planning home once
docs.text:
Read the project tooling map and active assignment before selecting an integration or creating records. Keep the plan, acceptance, questions and required approval receipt at the designated home. Respect project-owned fields and preserve human feedback.

Use the context recovery contract across session or model switches. Read current sources before resuming an old plan, preserve significant rationale when it arises and save a bounded handoff at the existing home. Old green checks and copied approval do not automatically apply after material scope, decision, contract or code changes.

For larger local work with no assigned system, use one work record. For a small fix, inspect, change and verify directly. If the designated system is unavailable, record the access limitation and prepare an unsent update in the current conversation; continue independent work without inventing synchronization or creating a competing source of truth. Resolve conflicting ownership before shared writes.

For planned work that needs approval, use local Plannotator review between Plan and Build when available. Comments go back to Plan; Build starts after the current revision is approved. The review UI does not choose or replace the project’s planning home. Choose a model and supported thinking variant for each phase when useful; carry the approved scope and evidence across model changes.

docs.title: Questions improve the assignment
docs.text:
Bundle related questions with a recommendation, impact and the needed decision. Route business questions to the Product Owner, design to the Technical Owner and operational questions to Operations. Preserve original answers as evidence. Continue independent work within scope while a consequential answer is pending.

Update the plan after a material increment or answer. Keep transient exploration and full tool logs out of routine comments; link detailed evidence instead.

docs.title: Decisions are recorded during delivery
docs.text:
Draft an ADR when a significant choice arises, while alternatives and reasons are available. The authorized decision maker accepts or rejects it. Preserve accepted rationale; a substantive replacement gets a new ADR and an explicit supersedes relation.

Decision acceptance, implementation, merge, deployment and observed business impact are separate states. Current knowledge describes behavior; historical ADRs explain choices. At iteration close, prepare one concise report linking outcomes, evidence, existing ADRs and material open work. Draft only missing significant decisions. Link the report from the designated project update. Each completed issue does not need an ADR.

docs.title: Keep context and coordination small
docs.text:
• Start with the project config and three workspace pages: goal/entry points, working agreement, stakeholders.
  • Load the active assignment and relevant knowledge, rather than the entire history.
  • Reuse loaded guidance; reread mutable feedback before updates.
  • Ask for a human decision when meaning, risk or authority requires one.
  • Delegate only when supported, authorized and useful; give each writer a bounded scope.
  • Archive completed work out of routine context and generate views from canonical sources.

Measure time to a reviewable increment, repeated questions, documentation effort and customer outcomes using an actual baseline. File counts and text volume do not prove value.

docs.title: Make quality observable
docs.text:
Provide the agent with reproducible setup, start and check commands, representative fixtures and access to the relevant UI, API or logs within its authorized scope. Turn acceptance criteria into checks at the affected boundary. Derive expected behavior from the requirement or contract, independently of the implementation. Use CI for repeatable quality rules; request human judgment for consequential tradeoffs.

Deliver small complete increments. Review evidence and the diff. For operational changes include the relevant rollout, recovery and post-deployment observation; keep unrun checks and unknown impact visible. Promote recurring defects into a focused regression check or a clarified rule instead of growing a universal instruction manual.

For a few comparable assignments, measure time to accepted result, human review effort, rework or escaped defects, and the intended user outcome. Compare model/effort or coordination changes against that baseline. Keep a change only when its benefit justifies its operating cost; token consumption alone cannot measure delivery quality.

docs.title: Keep tools replaceable
docs.text: Maintain the process and expertise once. Customer knowledge stays at the project-designated home, shared expertise in canonical catalog files, and host-specific discovery/permissions in generated adapters. Model changes do not rename project folders. Host changes require checking capabilities and effective permissions. See portability.

docs.title: What you can use today
docs.text:
The toolkit exports Jörg, Plan, Build, specialists and focused skills. It includes a local dashboard and a customer workspace starter. Your host runs models and tools and provides native delegation where supported. Provider choice controls whether inference is local or remote. The OpenCode 1 export can optionally configure Plannotator and separate Plan/Build models and variants. Review happens locally; installed-host behavior needs a local smoke check.

The starter includes a local graph generator and an existing-site Docusaurus guide. Its runner page is a design contract. Adopt the manual issue-to-PR flow first; recurring execution needs an implemented runner and authorized host capabilities.

Continue with runtime setup, the working contract or the worked assignment.

Canonical source: toolkit/OPERATING-MODEL.md.

docs.title: Must my repository use a .claude folder or change for every model?
docs.text: No. Keep shared rules in AGENTS.md, customer knowledge in workspace/ and reusable expertise in the canonical catalog. A model change within a host needs no folder change. Host tools have different discovery paths and permissions; exports generate those adapters from the same sources. See portability.

docs.title: Must every project use GitHub Issues or repository knowledge?
docs.text: No. Each project defines its tracker, planning home, code review, decision and knowledge locations in workspace/workspace.yml. Jira can own the plan while GitHub holds only the PR; Confluence or a repository can own knowledge. The customer starter uses GitHub as a worked example. Missing tool access means an unsent proposed update, not a new tracker.

docs.title: Which hosts have native exports?
docs.text: OpenCode 1, VS Code/Copilot and Claude Code. A portable export also provides Agent Skills and generic agent profiles; generic profile discovery remains host-specific. Permissions and review UI are not equivalent across hosts. See runtime setup and perform a local discovery check.

docs.title: Is it an OpenCode session orchestration plugin?
docs.text: No. It exports native agents, skills and commands. Delegation and session interaction come from the installed host. The dashboard manages files and does not launch agents.

docs.title: Can Plan and Build be customized?
docs.text: Yes. Edit their canonical profiles and re-export. OpenCode Plan has scoped edit permissions for work records; its shell/task tools are denied. Review the final merged host configuration and other installed tools before relying on a read-only boundary.

docs.title: Can I comment on and approve a plan before using another model for Build?
docs.text: Use the optional Plannotator plan review in OpenCode 1. Plan submits a concrete revision, receives comments and resubmits after requested changes. Build starts after actual approval. Separate model and supported variant fields configure the two phases; verify their selection in your installed Web version. The toolkit configures the external plugin; it neither proves runtime switching nor synchronizes GitHub issues.

docs.title: Must every task create a document?
docs.text: No. Small changes use the conversation and existing checks. Larger outcomes use one planning home: the project-designated work item for tracked delivery, or workspace/work/ for larger local work without that assignment. CSV is an export only.

docs.title: Is this website Docusaurus?
docs.text: The AI Agents catalog site uses MkDocs. The workspace starter integrates with a customer's existing Docusaurus site. Both publish views of canonical Markdown; compiled docs/ output stays separate from editable workspace sources.

docs.title: Does an accepted ADR prove delivery?
docs.text: It records the authorized decision maker's agreement. Implementation, verification, review, merge, deployment and observed impact each need evidence. Write significant decisions during delivery and link them at iteration close.

docs.title: Must I copy all the starter files?
docs.text: Start with the project YAML config, workspace entry page, working agreement and stakeholders. Adopt relevant instructions into the existing AGENTS.md. The worked files illustrate format; create real ADRs and knowledge pages when the assignment warrants them.

docs.title: Is the recurring local worker implemented?
docs.text: The manual host workflow, profile exports, dashboard and graph generator are available. The runner page is a design contract. Recurring processing needs an implementation and authorized tools for the customer's Project, issues and repositories.

docs.title: Does it upload my Obsidian vault?
docs.text: The toolkit has no remote vault service. An AI host can read an explicitly accessible vault using its own tools and provider configuration. Keep private notes and paths outside this public repository.

docs.title: Do Obsidian links open from OpenCode Web?
docs.text: The URI helper produces correctly encoded obsidian:// links. Clickability depends on the web renderer and Windows protocol registration. Copy the URI if it is filtered.

docs.title: How do I update profiles?
docs.text: Update the repository and re-export to the same dedicated destination. Edited or unmanaged files cause a clear error; integrate deliberately or choose another output.

docs.title: AI Agents project workspace
docs.text: This repository maintains a portable agent/skill catalog, runtime exporters and a local work-record toolkit. The goal is reliable collaboration from shared sources across people, sessions, models and hosts. Read the detailed workspace concept for the full information model, delivery flow, configuration, migration and publication boundary.

docs.title: Entry points
docs.text:
• Run this repository's workflow: setup, OpenCode startup and a repeatable process replay.
  • Pilot observation: actual local results and unverified boundaries.
  • Workspace configuration: actual repository locations and checks.
  • Working agreement: instructions, review and completion.
  • Stakeholders: accountable roles and permitted contact.
  • Operating model: outcomes and decision ownership.
  • Recovery contract: continue from current sources.
  • Decision index: rationale for repository-wide choices.
  • Iteration reports: report convention, created only when needed.

An assigned GitHub issue owns its current plan and acceptance; the PR owns implementation and checks. A direct maintenance request already represented by an open PR keeps its bounded plan and handoff there. A larger direct request without a tracker assignment may use one local workspace/work/ record. Local work and archives are ignored by default and are not published by the knowledge views. Do not copy private chat or customer notes here. General reusable instructions remain in toolkit/, agents/ and skills/.

Canonical source: workspace/README.md.

docs.title: Example outcomes
docs.text:
Outcome Start with Keep the result in Implement a Python API Jörg or Python Expert Existing code and one work record if useful Improve a frontend flow Frontend Expert Existing interface, contract and verification Reduce product uncertainty Product Manager One scoped experiment and acceptance criteria Maintain personal knowledge Second Brain The existing private PARA vault Review a risky change Code Reviewer Actionable findings with evidence Prepare a presentation Presentation Agent A rendered Marp deck when tooling is available Deliver a customer increment from a board Jörg with the customer's working agreement Assigned issue, linked PR and affected workspace knowledge Close an iteration Product Manager with decision owners One concise report linking outcomes, evidence and existing ADRs

For board-managed work, the issue owns the current plan. Use a local record when no existing assignment owns it. Follow the worked example through questions, review, decisions and iteration closeout.

Profiles do not imply access to accounts, devices or sessions. Configure tools in your host and keep public project artifacts separate from private knowledge.

docs.title: Why organize AI work this way?
docs.text:
Faster implementation makes clear assignments, decision rights and reusable knowledge more valuable. A team needs to find current evidence and continue another person's work without reconstructing a long chat.

The operating model gives each kind of information one home: a Project coordinates delivery, an issue holds its plan, a PR holds evidence, and the customer's repository preserves meaningful decisions and current knowledge.

Start with a clear outcome, the project tooling config and three workspace entry pages. Add an ADR when a significant choice arises; write a brief report at iteration close. Reuse customer systems, technology and review rules. Load focused context and archive completed work.

General profiles can improve across projects while customer facts stay with the customer. The worked assignment shows the handoffs; source ownership explains each component's responsibility.

docs.title: Project workspace: the shared memory for people and AI
docs.text:
For a short explanation you can share with a team and a practical first setup, start with Adopt the workspace. Use the project setup prompt to configure an existing project. This page remains the detailed contract behind those entry points.

Use workspace/ as the project's shared working context. It holds the tooling map, entry points, decision rationale and current knowledge, plus optional local work records. People and AI use the same sources. Another person or a fresh session must be able to continue an assignment without the previous conversation.

This concept combines the operating model, working contract, configuration and recovery contract. These documents provide focused operational instructions; this page explains how their parts fit together.

docs.title: 1. Outcomes and principles
docs.text:
• Preserve why a significant choice was made, including alternatives and consequences.
  • Keep one authoritative home for each fact and one live plan per assignment.
  • Load relevant context from shared sources instead of growing a mandatory chat history.
  • Make AI a sparring partner: inspect assumptions, propose alternatives and identify evidence that could change the recommendation. Work within the assigned decision rights.
  • Keep customer knowledge with the customer and general expertise in the agent catalog.
  • Scale ceremony to uncertainty and consequence. A clear small correction stays direct.

The workspace is a team convention, not a model memory API or a new project-management system. Existing customer methods remain valid, including their own planning process, Plan/Build/Review or another adopted method. Use an existing equivalent entry point when the project already has one.

docs.title: 2. Folder and information ownership
docs.text:
All paths below are relative to the project root. Create only the parts the project needs.

Path Purpose Update and publication rule AGENTS.md Entry instructions, commands and pointer to workspace config Preserve project rules; keep short workspace/README.md Outcome, scope and links to authoritative sources Reviewed project context workspace/workspace.yml Machine-readable tool and process mapping One configuration; no credentials workspace/working-agreement.md Authority, review, flow and completion policy Adopt with the responsible owner workspace/stakeholders.md Decision roles and permitted communication Use verified contacts within scope workspace/decisions/ Significant ADRs and their historical rationale Preserve accepted reasoning and replacement links workspace/knowledge/ Current domain, architecture and operational knowledge Update affected pages when behavior changes workspace/iterations/ Outcomes, learning and open follow-up Link evidence; no duplicate live task list workspace/work/ Optional local record for an otherwise unassigned larger outcome Local and ignored by default workspace/archive/ Completed local work records Local history, excluded from routine context workspace/generated/ Replaceable previews and derived output Ignored; never a source of truth workspace/exports/ Optional generated host bundles Ignored; edit canonical catalog sources

The --workspace CLI option still means the project root. For a project at /path/to/project, pass that root; the store writes workspace/work/ beneath it. Passing /path/to/project/workspace would create an unintended nested workspace.

The local store uses this conventional folder name. A customer can retain a different knowledge directory through the declared locations, but the store does not provide a configurable alternate record root. Resolve an existing conflicting workspace/ before using local records; adopting documentation never authorizes overwriting customer files.

docs.title: 3. One plan, even with several tools
docs.text:
Project arrangement Live assignment and plan Code and proof Durable knowledge GitHub Assigned issue; Projects owns adopted board fields Repository, PR and checks Project-selected repository or wiki Jira with GitHub Jira ticket; no mirror GitHub issue Linked GitHub PR and checks Repository ADRs and/or Confluence Split product and engineering planning Jira owns product/capacity; explicitly scoped engineering items own technical increments Linked repository changes per increment Shared customer-owned sources Larger local request with no assigned tracker One workspace/work/<slug>.md Local changes and actual checks Existing project documentation

For split planning, use a stable delivery-object reference and explicit parent/child relationships. Define ownership per field and work item before writing. Do not maintain two editable copies of the same live plan. A missing connector does not change ownership. Prepare an unsent proposed update and continue only independent authorized work.

docs.title: 4. The YAML contract
docs.text:
Use the GitHub example, Jira example or this repository's configuration. All use the same JSON Schema and validator.

Required version-1 fields retain the six authoritative locations, project name and working-agreement/stakeholder pointers. Optional sections add:

  • profile and method: project arrangement and chosen delivery method.
  • repositories: named code repositories, optional local paths and base branches.
  • planning: separate priority, iteration and engineering-status ownership when needed.
  • flow: actual board-state mapping, blocked property and completion policy.
  • handoff: the existing work-item section and a shared template.
  • labels and reviewers: adopted coordination labels and responsible reviewers.
  • commands and quality_gates: reproducible project commands and required checks.
  • actions: agreed action categories, still subject to real authorization and permissions.

The YAML is declarative. Validation makes no connection, creates no board or labels, executes no commands and grants no authority. Confirm actual access and adopted policy in the chosen host. Do not invent GitHub Project IDs, Jira fields or reviewer approval. Relative paths resolve from the project root, not from the configuration directory.

The older standalone v0.2 concept example used schema_version, sources and paths; it was explicitly a separate example schema. Map those ownership values into this contract rather than copying its YAML verbatim. Existing toolkit version-1 configs remain valid without the new optional sections. An explicitly linked project.yaml is supported; keeping it beside workspace.yml is rejected as ambiguous.

docs.title: 5. Initial project setup
docs.text:
1. Determine the outcome, scope, quality constraints and accountable people.
  2. Inspect the existing tracker, repositories, instructions, contracts and decisions.
  3. Adopt the minimum entry pages and map actual locations in the YAML. Preserve existing policies and private content; do not copy fictional customer details into production.
  4. Agree which actions are allowed within an assignment, which require a decision and which tools or credentials the host actually has.
  5. Record significant initial choices and unresolved assumptions. Architecture evolves during delivery; do not invent historical decisions or require all design up front.
  6. Validate the config and perform the host smoke check.
  7. Select one bounded real assignment and run the manual flow before adding orchestration.

docs.title: 6. Delivery and sparring
docs.text:
Start from an outcome and observable criteria. Inspect relevant constraints before proposing the smallest complete increment. When uncertainty matters, compare alternatives, state the recommendation and tradeoffs, and name what evidence would change it.

Follow the project's review policy. Routine reversible implementation details within the assigned scope can proceed. An incompatible API change, changed data meaning, material cost/security consequence or disputed architectural constraint needs the accountable role. Do not ask for every routine step or silently reinterpret consequential requirements.

Implement, exercise the affected behavior and link criteria to actual results on a specific revision. A second AI review is not automatically independent approval. Update affected knowledge and significant decisions as they arise. The iteration report links these outcomes and unresolved items; it is not the first place to reconstruct rationale.

Trigger Action Result New assignment or resumed session Read current sources and choose a bounded increment Current scope and next step Required decision or plan review Obtain the accountable owner's decision on the current revision Preserved decision or approval evidence Authorized increment Implement and verify criteria; save evidence and handoff Reviewable result on a known revision Changes requested Revise the affected increment and repeat relevant checks Updated result and feedback disposition Acceptance at the completion point Close work and link reusable learning Verified outcome, with impact still separately measured

docs.title: 7. Decisions, current knowledge and recovery memory
docs.text:
Question Read or update Why did we choose this approach? ADR with context, alternatives, evidence, decision and consequences What currently applies? Accepted decisions in scope and current contracts What is actually implemented? Code, tests and operational evidence What are we trying to change? Current assignment, criteria and human feedback Where do we continue? Bounded handoff in the existing planning home

Use stable ADR IDs and explicit statuses. A proposed replacement cannot revoke an accepted decision. A substantive replacement gets a new ADR, a supersedes relation and an updated old status; preserve the old reasoning. Correct factual metadata without silently rewriting accepted rationale. Resolve contradictions by scope and authority, not by the newest file timestamp or the current code alone.

Record useful outcomes and reasons, not private reasoning traces or full chat dumps. The workspace supports shared project memory; it does not make model-internal memory reliable or replace the authoritative sources.

docs.title: 8. Context loading and fresh sessions
docs.text:
Load the short entry, config, applicable rules and actual assignment first. Follow links to affected code, tests, contracts and decisions. Search the bounded project when a relevant source is missing; an absent link does not prove that no decision exists. Load full documents only as needed. Do not load the entire archive or every agent/skill.

Before resuming, compare the current sources with the last handoff: assignment revision, relevant commits, ADR status, current approval and tested criteria. Refresh affected context after material changes. An unrelated commit does not require rereading everything. Do not omit relevant constraints merely to satisfy an arbitrary token budget.

Save the bounded handoff after material increments and before a known pause or session/model switch. Include unsaved work and pending external writes. One current summary belongs inside the assigned work item or existing local record; the template file is not another running plan.

docs.title: 9. Flow, completion and failure recovery
docs.text:
Map Todo, In Progress, In Review and Done to the adopted board. Blocked is an additional property with reason, owner and resume condition; preserve underlying flow position and WIP. A team's existing equivalent mapping may differ when explicit.

For code, Engineering Done requires criterion evidence, required review and authorized integration at the agreed completion point. Acceptance, merge, deployment and measured impact remain distinct facts. Cancelled, duplicate and not-implemented closures do not count as delivered. An investigation can finish with a verified answer.

After a timeout, inspect the original system for the intended write before retrying. Git, trackers and review systems are not one atomic transaction. Reconcile partial effects and preserve intervening human edits. One writer owns an assignment or separate bounded scope. Multiple workers need an effective shared claim and recovery policy; an assignee field alone is not an atomic lock. Record each relevant repo revision and integration order for multi-repository work.

The toolkit implements local record persistence, stale-write protection and exports. It does not implement tracker polling, cross-system transactions, distributed claims or an agent/session runner. The runner example describes an integration contract rather than an installed service.

docs.title: 10. Publication and privacy
docs.text:
One directory can hold several information types without granting them the same audience. Local work/, archive/, generated/ and exports/ are ignored by default and excluded from the example knowledge graph and Docusaurus publication. Git ignore rules alone do not stop a website from reading files on disk.

The Docusaurus fragment publishes named root entry pages and the selected knowledge, decisions and iteration directories. Review that allowlist and sources before adopting it. Do not add local work directories to the site. Configuring workspace/ as a broad content source without exclusions would publish local notes. Keep secrets and personal material outside public repositories, and enforce the customer's access requirements on the published site.

docs/ remains generated Pages output in this repository. Its MkDocs site reads explicit canonical sources through the docs hook; it does not recursively publish the root workspace. The export manifest .ai-toolkit-manifest.json remains an adapter-ownership file so existing bundles retain protection against overwriting human edits. It is not a project-memory folder.

docs.title: 11. Moving existing local work
docs.text:
Stop agents, dashboards and editors that write records. Back up the project. Then run:

python3 tools/ai_toolkit.py work --workspace /path/to/project migrate --dry-run
python3 tools/ai_toolkit.py work --workspace /path/to/project migrate
python3 tools/ai_toolkit.py work --workspace /path/to/project list

Migration moves .ai/work/ and .ai/archive/ into workspace/ without changing file contents. It checks both destinations before moving anything, refuses existing target directories and rejects symlinks. It does not merge conflicts, rewrite relative links, move unknown .ai content or grant permission to disclose records. Resolve conflicts and update affected links deliberately. The empty old parent directory is removed; remaining unknown content is preserved and reported by legacy_directory_remaining.

Each directory move is a separate filesystem operation. If interrupted, inspect both locations and rerun after stopping writers; already-moved directories are left alone. This is not a distributed migration lock. The store reports remaining legacy records instead of hiding them or creating a second plan. Old ignored paths stay ignored during transition. Regenerate disposable previews and bundles under the new paths, then update host references deliberately; never delete edited bundles as part of a blind migration.

docs.title: 12. Evidence and adoption decision
docs.text:
Run the cold-session pilot on real authorized work. Test a relevant decision change, unavailable tracker and small bypass task. Separately exercise installed-host discovery, effective permissions, live API retries and competing writers before expanding autonomy.

The local observation records bounded recovery behavior, not broad productivity or installed-host reliability. Compare a few similar assignments for reconstruction effort, recovery errors, time to accepted outcome, review/rework and intended user impact. State model/host and process versions, raw evidence, failed attempts and unrun boundaries. Keep rules whose benefit exceeds their maintenance cost; improve repeatable tooling instead of continually enlarging prompts.

Canonical source: toolkit/WORKSPACE-CONCEPT.md.

docs.title: Agents

  • Give each skill a specific selection situation and observable result. Improve an existing skill before adding overlapping roles; keep shared process in the workflow.
  • Evaluate consequential instruction changes on a small realistic task, a missing-tool case and a task that should bypass the skill. Report observed behavior separately from structural validation; do not claim a model was tested if it was not.

docs.text: Keep the toolkit standard-library-only at runtime. Add meaningful unittest checks for persistence, export, API or permission changes. Update the applicable user guide. Documentation sources live in assets/mkdocs/; generated docs/ is maintained by the main workflow. Reference examples do not mandate a framework or architecture.

docs.title: Cold-session pilot
docs.text:
Adopt the project's actual rules and select an authorized bounded assignment. Do not use fictional issue numbers, sources or approvals as evidence in a real project.

  1. Session A reads the assignment and relevant shared context, performs a bounded step and saves the current handoff at the designated planning home.
  2. Preserve the actual code/check revisions, open questions, unsaved work and pending writes.
  3. Introduce an authorized relevant source change, or observe one that occurs naturally.
  4. Start a fresh Session B with only the assignment and shared-source entry. Do not provide the old chat, expected diagnosis or intended answer.
  5. Observe its source selection, applicable decisions, treatment of changed scope/approval, preservation of human feedback, next action and actual verification.
  6. Have a person check the result and record evidence, errors, recovery time and limits.

Also exercise an inaccessible designated tracker and a clear small edit. The first must not create a mirror plan or invent current state; the second must not add unnecessary process records. Further integration cases include timeout after write, competing workers, tracker outage, stale test evidence and duplicate/cancelled closure.

Report scenarios as not run, passed, failed or blocked. File snapshots exercise source reasoning but do not prove live API access, atomic claims or installed OpenCode/Claude behavior. Local validators check structure only. Keep each observation's model/host, process revision, artifacts and limitations so another evaluator can repeat the case.

docs.title: Local Docusaurus knowledge publishing
docs.text: These are integration instructions for an existing Docusaurus 3 website under website/. The starter does not contain a complete website, a deployed portal or a background runner.

docs.title: Source, route and output are separate
docs.text:
• Canonical Markdown: workspace/; people and AI edit these files through reviewed changes.
  • Website configuration: the existing website/ directory.
  • Docs plugin options: use docusaurus-workspace.cjs as an options fragment.
  • Website route: /workspace/; keep each knowledge record's slug stable.
  • Generated static output: Docusaurus defaults to website/build/. If root docs/ is reserved for your compiled GitHub Pages output, build into ../docs and keep that folder generated.

Never point the docs content plugin at a directory that also receives its compiled output. Check that an output directory contains only replaceable generated files before building into it.

docs.title: Keep local work outside publication
docs.text:
The options fragment allowlists root Markdown plus knowledge/, decisions/ and iterations/, and excludes local work/, archive/, generated/ and exports/. Merge this boundary with the customer's existing content rules. Do not replace it with a recursive all-Markdown include. The graph generator also skips those four local directories before reading files. Neither Git ignore rules nor a local folder name alone prevent a documentation plugin from publishing files on disk.

Review selected entry pages and derived JSON for the intended audience. This example configuration has no installed Docusaurus smoke-test result; verify the actual site and its access controls before publication.

docs.title: Enable Mermaid in the existing configuration
docs.text:
Install @docusaurus/theme-mermaid at the version matching the website's Docusaurus packages. Merge these top-level settings into the existing configuration; preserve all existing themes and other Markdown options:

markdown: {mermaid: true},
themes: ['@docusaurus/theme-mermaid'],

The docs fragment assumes website/ and workspace/ are sibling directories. If the website is at the repository root, use path: 'workspace' instead. If the website already reads another documentation source, preserve that plugin and add a separate @docusaurus/plugin-content-docs instance with id: 'workspace' and this fragment's options. Check that its route does not collide with an existing section.

docs.title: Generate the index and graph locally
docs.text:
From the repository root:

uv run examples/knowledge_graph.py workspace --json examples/knowledge-graph.json

Python 3.11+ and PyYAML are required. The script's dependency declaration lets uv resolve the parser; an existing environment with PyYAML can invoke it with Python directly. Generation reads only local Markdown. It makes no API requests and uses no graph service.

The generated page contains the record index, Mermaid diagram and clickable relationship table. Metadata is the source for both the page and JSON; edit the underlying records. The relations vocabulary is this starter's convention, not a MADR or Docusaurus standard. Sources link to original issues and PRs without importing their comments into the graph.

The checked-in generated example lets you inspect the output immediately. In a real project, regenerate before each website build and either commit generated views consistently or ignore workspace/knowledge-map.md and the generated JSON. Do not edit them manually.

docs.title: Build and inspect the existing website
docs.text:
After generation, from the existing website/ directory:

npm run build -- --out-dir ../docs
npm run serve -- --dir ../docs

These commands assume the usual package scripts map to docusaurus build and docusaurus serve. An existing build-output arrangement may use another directory. For branch-based GitHub Pages, keep its configured branch/folder; an artifact-based deployment may publish build/ without committing generated HTML. Publication follows the customer's agreed process.

docs.title: Scaling the graph
docs.text:
Start with the generated page and relationship table. When a product has many records, use a view by domain, status or the one/two-hop neighborhood of a selected ADR. The generated JSON can support an optional local React/Cytoscape component in Docusaurus; that interactive component is not implemented in this starter. Keep the accessible table. Do not hand-maintain an independent graph database or infer authoritative edges from text similarity.

Website access must match customer requirements. A private repository does not automatically make a published website private; configure hosting access separately. The JSON is published data if embedded in the website, so apply the same content boundary to it.

docs.title: Local runner contract
docs.text: This is a design contract, not implemented software or a started background job. The initial manual workflow can use Jorg in the customer's checked-out repository. A runner additionally needs authenticated access to the customer's Project, issues and repositories and an AI host capable of performing the authorized actions.

docs.title: Minimal loop
docs.text:
1. Read the configured customer Project. Select current-iteration Todo issues that meet the readiness condition assigned to the explicitly authorized worker identity; resume its existing active issue first.
  2. Compare Project field changes and issue/comment revisions with the local cursor. Load the active issue's current body, open questions and relevant new feedback.
  3. Claim one issue, create or resume its branch, and invoke the host with the issue and customer instructions. For multiple runner processes, use a shared claim mechanism.
  4. For a review-required assignment, submit the concrete plan revision and await actual approval. Persist the revision, review reference, notes and decision before invoking Build with its configured model/variant. A rejection returns to Plan; cancellation, timeout or unavailable review stays blocked. Do not infer approval from a successful call.
  5. Execute a bounded increment, verify it and publish a material update or draft PR. On a consequential blocker, record the question and await a relevant answer.
  6. At iteration close, prepare one report from actual accepted work and unresolved items. Upsert its draft using the iteration identifier so retries do not create duplicates.

docs.title: Efficiency and recovery
docs.text:
Use a small metadata query before loading issue bodies. Cache unchanged guidance; reread mutable assignments and feedback. Avoid loading every historical issue or archived decision. Back off while idle or waiting. Work only within the issue's agreed time and action budget.

Keep per-customer credentials, checkpoints and claim state in local protected configuration. Persist issue, branch and last processed comment identifiers for restart recovery. Deduplicate questions and closeout drafts. On resume, compare the current plan with its approved revision; material changes invalidate that approval and require review again. Keep credentials and model settings local; keep the plan and receipt in the customer issue. Reconcile the host's actual agent/model before implementation; no silent fallback to another model. Do not mark Done solely because the host returned successfully.

Project field editing permissions are separate from repository editing permissions. Report missing capabilities and prepare a reviewable result within the available scope.

Canonical source: templates/customer-workspace/examples/local-runner.md.

docs.title: Set up a shared workspace for people and AI
docs.text:
Copy the prompt below into a coding agent working in the target project. Make this toolkit checkout available as reference, or provide the current linked schema, guide and examples. Replace the bracketed input when known; the agent can discover the rest.

References: adoption guide, config contract, schema and starter. All are covered by the repository license.

docs.title: Prompt
docs.text:
Set up this project so people and AI can collaborate efficiently using a small shared workspace. Inspect the existing project first, then implement the necessary files and references. Preserve customer conventions and minimize ongoing documentation work. Use English for shared project artifacts and the user's language for conversation.

Inputs

  • Project: the current checkout, plus any repositories explicitly in scope.
  • AI Agents reference: [local toolkit checkout or repository URL and revision].
  • Known tracker/board: [URL if available; otherwise discover or ask].
  • Existing project instructions and the current user's authorization take precedence.

1. Understand the project

Read existing agent instructions, README, tooling configuration, relevant architecture and decisions, setup/test commands and CI. Inspect known repositories and tracker links with available read access. Determine the product outcome, relevant stakeholders and the sources of truth for current work and durable knowledge.

Do not invent URLs, contacts, branch names, command results or permissions. Resolve important missing information through a few specific questions; continue independent setup work where possible. Preserve human wording and check for intervening edits.

2. Use the actual configuration contract

Read the reference toolkit's current toolkit/PROJECT-CONFIG.md, toolkit/workspace.schema.json and matching YAML examples. Record the reference revision in the setup report. Reuse a compatible existing project map. Otherwise adapt one example as workspace/workspace.yml and link it from the project's agent entry point.

The version-1 contract uses six system/location mappings: work, review, knowledge, decisions, iteration_reports and communication, plus working_agreement and stakeholders. Use supported optional fields such as method, repositories, planning, flow, handoff, labels, reviewers, commands, quality_gates and actions only when useful. Do not invent a different schema or add unsupported tools or sources sections. If the reference cannot be loaded, describe the gap and continue read-only discovery; do not claim a configuration is compatible without its contract.

Map the real GitHub/GitLab repositories and review locations; use verified base branches. Map the GitHub Project or Jira project/board to the relevant work and planning ownership. If both systems exist, explain their distinct responsibilities and retain one live plan per work item. Relative paths resolve from the target project root.

Keep credentials and local account/connector configuration outside the YAML. The file declares locations and policy; it does not install an integration or grant authority.

3. Create only useful entry pages

Reuse existing equivalents or adapt these short starter pages:

  • workspace/README.md: product outcome, scope and important context links.
  • workspace/working-agreement.md: chosen method, planning home, quality gates, communication, decision rights and completion evidence.
  • workspace/stakeholders.md: accountable roles and permitted, verified contact routes.

Merge a concise pointer into existing agent instructions, such as AGENTS.md. Respect the host's actual discovery rules. Do not overwrite its instructions or assume that an arbitrary Markdown file is loaded automatically.

Do not copy fictional ADRs, reports, customer names or issue numbers into production. Create knowledge and decision pages when the work actually warrants them. Keep common skills in their central maintained source, with host exports treated as generated output.

4. Define how collaboration works

Keep the project's chosen method: BMAD, Plan/Build/Review or its established procedure. Do not introduce a second mandatory process beside it. A bounded assignment needs a specific work-item reference, outcome, acceptance criteria and responsible decision role. A board link alone is not authorization to process its backlog.

Document how the agent reads the assignment, keeps one concise current plan, asks consequential questions, implements a small complete increment and links actual evidence on a known revision. Derive expected checks from requirements and consumer behavior. Missing access produces an unsent proposed update, not a mirror issue or invented sync.

If plan approval is required, preserve feedback and approval for the actual revision. Use Plannotator only when available and adopted; record any manual review alternative. Configure separate Plan/Build models or thinking settings only through supported host options. A plan approval does not authorize merge or deployment.

Keep significant rationale in customer-owned ADRs as decisions arise. Update affected current knowledge with behavior changes. Iteration reports link verified outcomes and open work; they are not another live task list. Save a bounded handoff in the existing planning home so a fresh session can resume from current shared sources.

5. Respect action and publication boundaries

Record already agreed actions and actual access. Do not infer customer permission from a template value. During setup, do not post test comments, change tracker state, create boards, merge or deploy without separate authorization for those actions.

Customer knowledge stays in customer-owned systems. A personal PARA vault may keep authorized references and generalized learning, without becoming a customer-data mirror. Publish only selected durable knowledge. Keep local work, archives, generated bundles and private notes outside website content. Preserve an existing generated docs/ directory.

6. Validate and report

Validate the target YAML using the toolkit's actual validator and schema. Check local references and documented commands against the project; run appropriate agreed checks. Report separately what passed, what was only inspected and what remains unverified. Do not execute a command merely because it appears in a copied configuration.

Deliver the changed files, a concise information-ownership map, remaining questions and access gaps, and one proposed real pilot assignment. Prepare a reviewable change through the existing contribution workflow. Stop at the project's agreed review boundary.

Keep the setup small. No empty folder trees, duplicate trackers, copied chat histories or large policy manuals without a concrete need.
